race.name: GFNY Ventura
race.tagline: Eighty-seven miles from the Pacific through Santa Paula and Ojai, with 6,500 feet of climbing and an eight-mile Dennison Grade.

vitals.start_format: Mass-start competitive long course with chip timing
vitals.registration: Online through the official GFNY race site
vitals.feed_zones: Official GFNY aid stations with hydration, food, technical, and medical support
vitals.cutoff_time: See current race guide and official course rules
route_options: Recreational medium route: see official race site

climate.primary: Mild coastal spring with inland heat exposure
climate.description: April can begin cool and marine near Ventura, then warm inland around Santa Paula and Ojai. Sun, dry air, and coastal wind can all appear in the same race.

terrain.surface: Paved Ventura County roads through coastal, agricultural, and mountain terrain.
features: A rolling opening from downtown Ventura to Santa Paula
Dennison Grade: eight miles and 1,300 feet of climbing
A long, gentle descent into Ojai Valley
Coastal exposure and accumulated climbing on the return

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: An excellent first-edition course with serious climbing and easy Southern California access. Inaugural execution and low established prestige prevent a higher tier.

key_climbs: A rolling opening from downtown Ventura to Santa Paula
Dennison Grade: eight miles and 1,300 feet of climbing
A long, gentle descent into Ojai Valley
Coastal exposure and accumulated climbing on the return
climb_profile.king_of_mountain: Dennison Grade, an eight-mile climb whose moderate average hides 1,300 feet of sustained gain and ramps up to seven percent.

course_description.character: The long route leaves the Pacific, crosses the agricultural interior, and stacks 6,500 feet of elevation across a broad Ventura County loop. Dennison Grade is the named centerpiece, but the race is an all-day climbing and pacing problem rather than a single-climb event.
course_description.signature_challenge: Dennison Grade, an eight-mile climb whose moderate average hides 1,300 feet of sustained gain and ramps up to seven percent.

logistics.airport: Santa Barbara Airport (SBA) is closest; Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) offers the most flights and is about 70 miles southeast.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in downtown Ventura near Mission Park to simplify packet pickup and race morning. Book early for coastal weekend rates.
logistics.transport: Use official race-week instructions for packet pickup, start access, and bike transport.
logistics.food: Downtown Ventura has abundant restaurants and groceries. The course's duration makes a practiced high-carbohydrate plan more important than a large pre-race dinner.

history.origin_story: GFNY announced its first Ventura edition in April 2026, selecting a Pacific-to-Ojai loop for an inaugural April 11, 2027 race.
history.reputation: A high-potential inaugural event with a mature route concept but no execution history yet.

biased_opinion.summary: The long route leaves the Pacific, crosses the agricultural interior, and stacks 6,500 feet of elevation across a broad Ventura County loop. Dennison Grade is the named centerpiece, but the race is an all-day climbing and pacing problem rather than a single-climb event.
weaknesses: Southern California lodging can be expensive
Wide climate range complicates equipment choices
biased_opinion.bottom_line: One of the strongest new U.S. GFNY courses: long enough, mountainous enough, and specific enough to justify dedicated preparation.

final_verdict.one_liner: Eighty-seven miles from the Pacific through Santa Paula and Ojai, with 6,500 feet of climbing and an eight-mile Dennison Grade.
final_verdict.should_you_race: One of the strongest new U.S. GFNY courses: long enough, mountainous enough, and specific enough to justify dedicated preparation.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY Walnut Creek for a summit finish, or Levi's GranFondo for a longer established Northern California challenge.
